stem: After a medication error, a nurse completes the organization's patient-safety event report. What is the primary purpose of this reporting process?

options.A: Automatically assign disciplinary action to the staff member involved
options.B: Replace the need for immediate clinical management of the patient
options.C: Support organizational learning, identify system vulnerabilities, and guide safety improvement
options.D: Serve as the patient's routine clinical progress documentation

rationale: AHRQ describes patient-safety event reporting as a core method for detecting safety events and quality problems and emphasizes using reports within a larger patient-safety system to learn from events and improve system performance. A blame-focused approach can inhibit reporting and safety improvement. Event reporting does not replace immediate patient care or routine clinical documentation.
educational_objective: Explain that patient-safety event reports are used for organizational learning and system-level safety improvement rather than automatic blame or replacement of clinical care.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: Reporting Patient Safety Events; CANDOR Module 4: Event Reporting, Event Investigation and Analysis
source_version_date: PSNet primer reviewed 2025; current AHRQ CANDOR module accessed 2026
source_locator: PSNet Reporting Patient Safety Events > Background; CANDOR Module 4 > Event Reporting Culture and Key Elements
source_claim_supported: Event reporting systems help detect safety events and quality problems and support learning and system improvement; blame-focused approaches inhibit reporting and improvement.
correction_summary: Removed the overbroad assertion that every incident report is categorically separate from every medical record under all systems and jurisdictions. Reframed the item around AHRQ's directly supported universal purpose: organizational learning and patient-safety improvement.
audit_findings: C is the AHRQ-supported purpose. A conflicts with a learning/Just Culture approach; B confuses reporting with immediate clinical response; D confuses an internal safety-reporting process with routine clinical documentation. No second answer remains.
